verified_claims.claim: July retail and food-services sales were $763.6 billion, down 0.6% month over month and up 5.0% year over year.
The reported 90% sampling-error interval for the monthly change was plus or minus 0.4 percentage point.
July category changes included nonstore -2.2%, autos -1.8%, gasoline stations -0.9%, restaurants +0.5%, clothing +1.9%, general merchandise +0.3%, and ex-autos-and-gas -0.2%.
Comparable early-May individual income-tax refunds rose from $274.979 billion in 2025 to $324.757 billion in 2026, while the average refund rose from $2,939 to $3,276.
The aggregate refund difference was $49.778 billion.
July headline CPI rose 0.1% month over month and 3.4% year over year; core CPI rose 0.2% month over month and 2.5% year over year.
The FOMC held the federal-funds target range at 3.5%-3.75% on July 29 in a 9-3 vote, with three members preferring a quarter-point increase.
Real GDP grew at a 1.5% annual rate in the Q2 2026 advance estimate.
The next advance retail-sales release is scheduled for September 16, 2026.
The July decline was the largest monthly drop since May 2025 and came against a professional consensus for a small gain.

analysis_not_numeric_authority: The refund bridge ending is the best organizing explanation for the July downshift.
The category mix indicates moderation rather than household capitulation.
Retail margins and promotion intensity may weaken before nominal sales collapse.
The combined retail and inflation data widen the Federal Reserve's waiting zone.
